MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 24, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on October 24, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 19, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Threat to Public Services or Facilities. Consultation with City of Mission Viejo Cyber
  Security/Video Operations Manager; City Attorney.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9): City of Mission Viejo v. State of California, DOF.

City Council Minutes  1  October 24, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two Closed Session matters. They
received an update and gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to the Winners of the “Why I Love Mission Viejo” Contest

  Mayor Bucknum presented prizes to contest winner Christine Sakata and runner-up Matt
  Whitcomb. Runner up Koshi Tagawa was unable to attend the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Margot Ferron, M.V.: invited the community to a “Stand up for Texas” comedy night on Friday,
October 27 at 7:30 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. The show is a fundraiser to
help rebuild a middle school in Port Aransas, Texas, which was heavily damaged by Hurricane
Harvey. Tickets are $15 each or $25 for a reserved seat and can be purchased online at
mvactivities.com or at the front desk at the Murray Center.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she worked for the City for eight years while serving on the City
Council and she was denied health care benefits that others received.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with illegal parties and frequent late night drug use
activity at Cordova Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  October 24, 2017
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of October 10, 2017, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 29, 2017 in the Amount of $2,926,718.47

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 6, 2017 in the Amount of $564,693.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2017

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2017

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2017

  Received and filed.

8.  2018 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events LLC to hold the 2018 Orange

9.  Conflict of Interest Code

  Adopted Resolution 17-48 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code.

10.  Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Traffic Signal Synchronization (CIP 18236)

  (1) Authorized issuance of a purchase order to DKS Associates, Inc., in an amount not to
  exceed $141,800 for design engineering services for the subject project; and (2) adopted

City Council Minutes  3  October 24, 2017
   Resolution 17-49 Amending the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Budget for Costs Related to
  Capital Improvement Project 18236.

11.  Cordova Park Play Area Renovations - CIP 306

  (1) Awarded contract to Micon Construction, Inc. for the Cordova Park Play Area

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

13.  Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract for California Public Employees’
  Retirement System to Implement Government Code section 20516(a)

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt
  Ordinance 17-325 Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract Between the City Council
  of the City of Mission Viejo and the Board of Administration of the California Public
  Employees' Retirement System.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-51 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.
City Council Minutes  4  October 24, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

16.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum deferred her report to a future Council Meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

17.  Intent to Transition from At-Large to District-Based Elections, Outlining Specifics
  Steps to be Undertaken to Facilitate the Transition, and Estimating a Timeframe for
  Action

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she doesn’t see a need for districts because she was one of
  the two people elected to the Mission Viejo City Council who is Latino and she served for
  eight years. Mrs. Reavis said she resents what the Shenkman and Hughes law firm is trying
  to do and she volunteered to be on a committee to address this matter.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: said that he was amused to see an argument that the City might be in
  violation the California Voting Rights Act. He noted that former City Council candidate
  Joe Chavez lost the elections in which he ran due to the fact he did not spend any money
  in his campaigns, not due to block voting. Mr. Gilbert stated that to the best of his
  knowledge, no Latino has ever been discouraged from running for office in Mission Viejo.

  Steve Serra, M.V.: submitted a written comment in opposition to the concept of district
  elections in Mission Viejo.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs expressed his interest in adding the word “consider” before
  transition in the Resolution title. By consensus, the City Council agreed to the amendment.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to adopt Resolution
  17-52 Declaring its Intent to Consider Transition from At-Large to District-Based
  Councilmember Elections, Outlining Specific Steps to be Undertaken to Facilitate the
  Transition, and Estimating a Timeframe for Action Pursuant to Elections Code Section 10010.

City Council Minutes  5  October 24, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell stated that he is looking forward to the research that is presented at the
upcoming public workshops on district based elections. He said that he was intrigued to hear
resident Larry Gilbert announce that at least two Mission Viejo Council Members were
Latino/Latina during the period of 1998 through 2004. Council Member Goodell outlined his
attendance at recent events including the ceremony for resident and volunteer Sharon Cody whose
name was added to the City’s Wall of Recognition; the Chamber of Commerce Mixer which the
City hosted at Melinda Park; and the Walk Against Drugs and Emergency Preparedness Fair.
Council Member Goodell announced that earlier in the day, he attended the Orange County
Association of Governments Municipal Law Seminar where he received a briefing on the new
laws that Governor Brown has signed. He said there are opportunities and there are difficulties that
cities will have to deal with in terms of the new state legislation, particularly in the area of housing.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley added her commendations on the Walk Against Drugs and Disaster
Preparedness Expo and stated that it was a fantastic event again this year. She announced that she
has been attending monthly Drug Prevention Coalition meetings since the committee was formed
in July and, at the last meeting, the Coalition members prepared packets for destroying medications
at home. To create the do-it-yourself packets, she said people can put their unwanted pills in a
baggie, add hot water or coffee and some kitty litter or dirt. The pills dissolve in the baggie and
can be put in the trash. Council Member Kelley announced that there is a National Prescription
Take Back Day event on Saturday, October 28 from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. in the parking lot at
city hall. She outlined additional events including Hometown Halloween on October 28 from 4:00
to 7:00 p.m. at Oso Viejo Park and a free flu shot clinic on Friday, November 3 from 10:00 a.m.
to 2:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center. She noted that the flu shots
are for adults 18 years and older and there will be drive-through service for those who have
mobility issues. Council Member Kelley referred to the discussion earlier in the evening about a
loud party at a park and she reminded the public that the City does have a multiple call ordinance
which allows the Sheriff’s deputies to provide a notice to the resident that they will be assessed a

City Council Minutes  6  October 24, 2017
 fee for second and future calls. She noted that the ordinance has been very effective and according
to the Chief of Police Services, there were no multiple call incidents over the summer.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked Margot Ferron for all that she has done to organize the Stand up
for Texas comedy event and apologized for having to miss it. He said he was also sorry to miss
resident Sharon Cody’s induction for the City’s Wall of Recognition but he had been invited to a
dinner that Orange County Tax Assessor Claude Parrish hosted for all of the County Assessors in
the State. Council Member Raths thanked the City Manager for briefing him and Council Member
Goodell on the issues that business owner Ryan Farsai has brought before the City Council and he
said he hopes there will be a resolution soon. Noting that he is very involved in veteran matters,
he has been following the City of Irvine’s efforts to build a Veteran’s Cemetery. He said there was
a dispute with the original location and the Irvine City Council decided, on a 3-2 vote, to move the
cemetery to an area where the land can be easily graded and they can start putting veterans to rest.
Council Member Raths announced that the groundbreaking for the cemetery will be held on Friday,
October 27 and it means a lot that the City of Irvine is doing this. He said the people who are out
circulating petitions to have the cemetery moved back to its original location are making
unnecessary efforts as the majority are comfortable with the new location. Council Member Raths
asked the City Manager to provide him a map of the City that highlights all of the Homeowners
Associations (HOAs) because he is starting to get complaints from residents who are not in an
HOA and feel that their neighborhoods are getting run down. He asked if he could ride along with
a Code Enforcement officer and learn more about how HOAs work, and how the City keeps the
land and homes looking nice.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs noted that the Battalion Chief who was in attendance earlier in the meeting
was called away to a brush fire in the City of Orange. He said that his colleagues and residents
may have heard and read stories about possible negligence with Canyon Fire 2 and he said that all
of the claims are currently being investigated. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that Orange
County Fire Authority is going through their communication logs and developing a timeline from
the first report of the fire until its closure. He said there will soon be a determination and he looks
forward to seeing that report.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum stated that the Walk Against Drugs was terrific and the guest speaker, Josh
Stevens, grew up in Mission Viejo. He gave a great message about how he lives a drug free life
working in the music industry in Hollywood. She said she has heard residents say that they wish
we still had a City parade and she noted that the Walk Against Drugs is a parade. She suggested
that for future Walks, a high school drum line could lead the parade. Mayor Bucknum noted that
she introduced Jody Barber at the event and Jody has been very involved in drug prevention in the
community. Ms. Barber is interested in doing a tree dedication in Mission Viejo and the Mayor
asked staff to take a look at the possibility of doing that. She also reminded residents of the City’s
Veterans Day Ceremony on November 11 at 2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center, followed
City Council Minutes  7  October 24, 2017
 by the Chamber of Commerce State of the City gala at 6:00 p.m. at the Arroyo Trabuco Golf
Course. Mayor Bucknum said that the State of the City event will focus on women in leadership
and veterans and the Chamber has scholarships for veterans who may need help getting a ticket.
She also impressed that residents do not have to attend the event to see the State of the City video
as it will be shown at the December 12 City Council Meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:31 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 14, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 14, 2017

City Council Minutes  8  October 24, 2017
